note: Research backtest (Oct 9, 2026): every idea fit on 2024 and tested on 2025, FBS vs FBS games from week 2 on, each team's numbers rebuilt only from games played before each matchup. Lower average miss (points per game) is better.

matchupCorr: QB recent form after a QB change
market: Timing is where a model earns its keep: when the Data Rating disagreed with the OPENING line by 4+ points, the line moved toward the model 66% of the time in 2025 (74% in 2024), but against the CLOSING line the model's side won only 51%. Lines absorb what the model knows by kickoff, so beating the close (CLV) is the honest scorecard.
Home teams beat the closing spread by about 0.85 points per game in both 2024 and 2025: a hint the market slightly underrates home field. Suggestive, not proven (about 2 standard errors).
Mixing 20–30% model with 70–80% closing line lowered the 2025 miss slightly (11.83 → 11.80): the model holds a little information the close doesn't.
totals: Totals: a pace × efficiency scoring environment did not beat the closing over/under. One pattern repeated in both years: when both offenses rate as efficient, games went slightly UNDER the total (corr −0.10 in 2024, −0.06 in 2025). Overs hit 51% in 2024 and 49% in 2025.
verdict: What predicts college football: a good preseason prior, this season's results with turnover luck partly removed, and success rate. Player matchups, travel and rest add nothing measurable once the line is known. The Player Model now uses that Data Rating in place of v1's EPA-only unit power.
sources: Action Network & Football Study Hall (turnover luck, wind, byes)
live2026: Live check on 2026 weeks 2–5 (220 games the model never saw): Data Rating 12.58, in-season results only 14.33, closing line 11.00. Same ordering as the backtest.
caveat: Honest caveat: the final settings (prior worth 2 games, half-strength luck, which inputs to drop) were chosen after seeing 2025 results, so 12.14 is slightly optimistic (by about 0.05 points). The 2026 check is clean.
